---
argmap-version: 0.2
title: "Concept: author locally, propagate globally"
description: "Five claims and three steps in one chain, with no line joining the top of the map to the bottom. You author one number at a time, on one node, in the language of that node alone. The solve then answers for the whole document at once: put a number on the middle claim and the claim above it moves, the claim below it moves, and the two roots three steps away move too. Nothing was edited between them, and nothing had to be, because a solved value is a property of the whole constraint set rather than of any one line."
---

# ===========================================================================
# The teaching point is the ABSENCE of a line. @heat and @mission are the two
# ends of this map and no evidence mentions both. A reader who moves the
# middle claim sees both ends move anyway, in opposite directions from the
# handle: forward along the arrows, and backwards against them.
#
# Backwards is the half that surprises people. @water is a PREMISE of $life,
# so a low conclusion is evidence against the premise, and the solve says so
# without anyone authoring a line that runs that way.
#
# Residual discipline (D36 rule 3): the two frontier roots @heat and @salts
# carry pins because nothing concludes into them. @water, @microbes and
# @mission are all concluded into, so they carry no pin and no check: this
# file asserts nothing about how likely they are, which is what makes the
# movement in the tour legible as the solve's own work.
#
# The Mars content is a plausible-sounding fiction chosen because the chain
# is easy to hold in the head. Do not cite it.
# ===========================================================================

@heat [Radiogenic heating keeps the Martian subsurface above freezing] 0.6: a frontier root, so the number on it is an authored pin  # tour: global-integration
@salts [Dissolved perchlorates depress the freezing point enough to matter] 0.7: the other root

@water [Liquid water persists below the surface]:  # tour: global-integration
$warm [heat and salts are jointly what keeps brine liquid] 0.75 @water | @heat AND @salts: linked, not convergent: warmth alone freezes at the wrong depth and salt alone does nothing without the heat

@microbes [Subsurface microbial life exists on Mars]:  # tour: global-integration
$life [liquid water is the prerequisite everyone agrees on] 0.8 @microbes | @water:

@mission [The next lander should carry a life-detection package]:  # tour: global-integration
$fund [worth the mass if the target might really be there] 0.7 @mission | @microbes: an instrument that looks for life is cheap next to the launch that carries it

# ---- what to watch, and why it is not a bug -------------------------------
# Solved 2026-09-08 (the default reference G, D161; solve_map.py):
#   @heat 0.600   @salts 0.699   @water 0.657   @microbes 0.763   @mission 0.767
# With a reader override of @microbes to 0.05 (--override microbes=0.05):
#   @heat 0.598   @salts 0.698   @water 0.219   @microbes 0.051   @mission 0.518
# (Under the retired uniform reference, --reference d36, 2026-08-04: as
# authored 0.597 / 0.697 / 0.505 / 0.627 / 0.718; with the override 0.578 /
# 0.677 / 0.159 / 0.088 / 0.529.)
#
# Three things in that second row are worth naming.
#
# 1. @water fell by two thirds of its value with no line pointing at it from
#    the handle. That is the backwards half: the reader's number is a claim
#    the map has to meet, and doubting the premise is the cheapest way.
# 2. @mission fell too, and @water and @mission share no edge at all.
# 3. The two roots barely moved (0.002 each). They are point pins, and a
#    point is held at about 200 flips (D161 item 2), so the retreat lands on
#    the unpinned claims in between: what bends is what the authors held
#    least firmly. The reader's own 0.05 is met (0.051, inside the 0.01
#    tolerance); under the retired reference the map held it at 0.088.
